The test image shows dark brown/reddish-brown discoloration concentrated on the petiole/stem junction area, with leaves remaining green. Key features: dark necrotic browning along the petiole, hairy stem tissue visible.

Top candidates: Anthracnose (brown spots on petioles/stems), Diaporthe (black pycnidia on stems), Phytophthora (dark stem discoloration). Let me compare reference images.

Now let me analyze what I've observed across all references:

**Test image key features:**
- Dark brown/reddish-brown discoloration covering the entire petiole (leaf stalk)
- Discoloration runs longitudinally along the petiole from where it meets the main stem
- Leaves remain green — only the petiole is affected
- No leaf spots, no root symptoms, no fruiting bodies clearly visible

**Comparison summary:**
- **Anthracnose**: Specifically mentions "brown cankers on petioles causing defoliation" — matches well, but reference images showed mostly pod lesions and dried material
- **Diaporthe**: The bottom-left reference image shows a green plant with an elongated brown longitudinal lesion along the stem — visually the closest match to the test image
- **Phytophthora**: Dark stem discoloration but extends from soil line upward, with wilted/dead leaves typically remaining attached
- **Cercospora**: Purple/bronze leaf discoloration, reddish-purple lesions on petioles — possible, but test image shows more brown than purple
- All others (Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, SDS, Brown Stem Rot, rust, mildew) clearly don't match

The brown longitudinal lesion on the petiole with green healthy leaves remaining attached is most consistent with **Diaporthe** (pod and stem blight). The Diaporthe reference image (bottom-left panel) shows the identical pattern: elongated brown lesion on a green stem with normal green leaves still attached.
